chapter_title: Chương 229: 0230 Trường Quay Hòn Đá Nổi Giận

segments.title: Chương 229: 0230 Trường Quay Hòn Đá Nổi Giận
segments.content:
In 2006, Shancheng was already showing the early makings of a 3D fantasy city.

Chen Guiliang and Bian Guanyue arrived in the afternoon and arranged to meet Guan Zhiqiang, Li Yulin, and Wang Yu near the station.

"Huo huo huo huo…"

The man himself had yet to appear, but his familiar, bizarre laugh already carried over.

Guan Zhiqiang still had that oafish look, but unlike before, he wasn't constantly looking down. He held a folding fan in his hand, fanning himself frantically as he walked over. Not only was his face covered in sweat, but his T-shirt was also soaked through.

Seeing him on the verge of heatstroke, Chen Guiliang felt a few degrees hotter out of thin air.

"Great Hero Chen, long time no see!"

Guan Zhiqiang opened his arms, seemingly wanting to give Chen Guiliang a bear hug.

Chen Guiliang quickly pushed him away. "Get lost, don't touch me!"

"Huo huo huo huo huo huo…"

Guan Zhiqiang laughed loudly, wiped the sweat from his face with his hand, flicked it away, and then used his shirt to dry his damp palm.

Li Yulin and Wang Yu were standing nearby.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Have you guys been waiting all this time in such hot weather?"

Li Yulin said, "We just had a bowl of liangxia and a bowl of liangfen. If you hadn't come soon, I would have died from the heat."

Bian Guanyue greeted Guan Zhiqiang and Li Yulin, then walked over to chat with Wang Yu.

Guan Zhiqiang asked, "Where are we going to hang out?"

"Around Jiefangbei and Chaotianmen," Chen Guiliang said.

Li Yulin said, "Let's take the light rail. A lot of the buses don't have AC, and the plastic seats are hot enough to fry an egg."

This year, both the Chuan and Yu regions were suffering from a major drought, and the heat was unbearable even in early summer.

Some cities and counties had even been in a drought from March all the way until it was time to fill out college applications. The rolling mountain ranges had turned directly from green to yellow. Forget the wild grass, even the trees had withered and died!

Leaving the long-distance bus station, Chen Guiliang was struck by the sight of internet cafes near the station, all with posters for *Zhengtu* displayed in prominent locations.

It was the same in Rongcheng; wherever there was an internet cafe, there was a promotional poster for *Zhengtu*.

Shi Yuzhu was really throwing money around!

The moment they boarded the light rail, it was instantly cool.

They went straight from the bus station to Chaotianmen, perfectly avoiding Line 2, the line that passes through a building.

Bian Guanyue had never been to Shancheng, and it was her first time on a light rail. She pressed her face to the window, finding everything novel.

"Great Hero Chen," Guan Zhiqiang said secretively, "Li Jun is also playing *Reign of Sovereigns*. Seems like he's already topped up over ten thousand yuan, spending all his saved-up lucky money. He even tried to borrow money from me a while back, but there's no way in hell I'd lend him any. That dumbass never pays back his debts."

Chen Guiliang smiled. "I'll try to talk to him someday. He shouldn't get too obsessed with games."

"Huo huo huo," Guan Zhiqiang just laughed.

Chen Guiliang asked Li Yulin, "How have you been lately?"

"Same old," Li Yulin said. "Wang Yu and I are both in Tier 2 universities. The schools aren't too strict, and the courses aren't very demanding. Damn, our school is even copying the Super Girl auditions, saying the top ten from our campus can advance to the Yuzhong district competition."

"And then?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Li Yulin said, "I paid a 60 yuan registration fee and sang one song during the audition. And then that was it. I went to ask what happened, and they told me I didn't pass the audition… Fuck! It was just a scam to get money!"

Chen Guiliang didn't comfort him, but instead burst out laughing at his misfortune.

This year, many colleges and universities across China were holding talent shows, even Tsinghua and Peking University. It was all due to the influence of last year's Super Girl.

Among them were quite a few school clubs that used campus singing competitions to scam registration fees.

Li Yulin had been the artistic type back in high school, always keeping a guitar by his bed. He had a dream of becoming a star, so getting scammed out of a few dozen yuan was perfectly normal.

"I told him it was a scam, but he wouldn't believe me," Wang Yu couldn't help but complain.

Li Yulin couldn't argue, so he could only say, "I'm not upset about being scammed out of the money. A few dozen yuan is nothing. I'm just pissed about being treated like an idiot!"

Bian Guanyue said, "It's okay, I think you have a great voice. I still remember you singing 'You in My Life' at the New Year's party in our senior year."

"I used to be pretty good, but I haven't practiced much since starting university."

Li Yulin was quite proud at the mention of the past.

He had won Wang Yu over by singing. Now, although they had occasional squabbles, their relationship was still very strong.

They had even met each other's parents last Spring Festival.

They agreed to get married after graduation and work hard together in Shancheng. Their families could chip in a few tens of thousands of yuan, but they would have to earn the rest of the money for a house themselves.

Li Yulin said with a sigh, "High school was still the best. I feel a bit tired now. Tutoring on weekends, part-time jobs at school during the week. Maybe things will get easier after graduation when I find a proper job."

Wang Yu looked at her boyfriend with a hint of heartache. In fact, she also worked part-time.

This young couple had already entered奋斗模式 early.

In comparison, Guan Zhiqiang had it the easiest; his life path had already been planned out for him by his elders.

The group chatted about interesting things from their high school days, and Li Yulin would occasionally point outside, introducing the landmark buildings they passed along the way to Chen Guiliang.

"This is Qixinggang. I hear it's often haunted," Li Yulin said.

Guan Zhiqiang was surprised. "Even your school knows that Qixinggang is haunted?"

Li Yulin said, "Who doesn't? This is where Zhang Xianzhong killed people. When the city expanded during the Republic era, they moved hundreds of thousands of graves from Qixinggang."

Guan Zhiqiang said, "I have a classmate who came to Qixinggang to hang out at night, and he heard ghostly wails in the middle of the night. Scary as hell!"

"Hahaha!"

Chen Guiliang was amused.

In a flash, they arrived at Jiefangbei and got off nearby.

Since the weather was just too hot, they ducked directly into an internet cafe to enjoy the air conditioning.

"Let's play *Audition Online* together!" Guan Zhiqiang strongly suggested.

Chen Guiliang went along with it, registering an account with Bian Guanyue.

Guan Zhiqiang, this fat and oafish-looking guy, was surprisingly an expert at *Audition Online*, and he had even topped up to buy a nice outfit.

"Clack clack clack clack…"

Guan Zhiqiang furiously tapped the keyboard, his fingers seeming to blur. He would even occasionally stand up and dance along with his in-game character.

Not only did he dance, he also sang along.

When he encountered a Korean song he didn't know the words to, he would just hum along with the melody.

The sight was too beautiful for Chen Guiliang to watch.

Bian Guanyue and Wang Yu covered their mouths, giggling, both amused by Guan Zhiqiang.

Li Yulin couldn't help but roast him, "Guan Zhiqiang, you should have entered the talent show. You'd sing and dance, and if any judge didn't let you pass, you'd just keep singing and dancing until you made them die of laughter."

"Huo huo huo huo…"

Guan Zhiqiang didn't seem to catch the sarcasm, taking it only as a compliment, and even started dancing more energetically on the spot.

They stayed at the internet cafe until evening, when the temperature had dropped a little.

Guan Zhiqiang was very familiar with the area and led them to a nearby place for old-school hot pot.

Once they got to the hot pot restaurant, Chen Guiliang made a phone call.

While they were happily eating their hot pot, a chubby middle-aged man hurried in, holding a phone to his ear and looking around.

"Here!"

Chen Guiliang stood up and waved.

The chubby man asked uncertainly, "The little boy under the streetlight?"

Chen Guiliang shook his hand and offered a business card, "My name is Chen Guiliang."

The chubby man didn't even need to look at the card. He had already remembered who Chen Guiliang was and quickly presented his own card with both hands. "My name is Zhu Mingyao, a reporter for the Shancheng Evening News."

Zhu Mingyao had made connections with the Beijing media through an article titled "Why Should Free Textbooks for Impoverished Students Be Only Black and White?"

It was about the free textbooks provided by the state to students in poor western regions.

But when the textbooks were distributed, they turned out to be entirely in black and white, a situation that affected several provinces and municipalities in the west.

Zhu Mingyao wrote an article reporting on the matter, which sparked a heated nationwide discussion.

"These are my friends," Chen Guiliang said, introducing Li Yulin and the others.
